answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral in escrow, so splitting control across k coordinated identities does not dilute accountability: correlated equivocation triggers penalties that scale as O(k²). Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation limits recovery of slashed stake. Thus a swarm cannot treat identities as a haven; its apparent pearl of independence becomes a liability exposed on the shared terrace of the public ledger.
